notes.summary: Fresh whole-packet audit and bounded evidence; source and reader qualifications identified. These observations are not correctness grants.
notes.detailedSummary: All 68 current bindings, 15 historical author-owned entries, 54 input origins and 54 author-local copies matched independently. The actual FINAL contains nine notes, whose texts differ from the expanded versions. The standalone reader is exactly reconstructed by appendix inlining and font substitutions, but its embedded G331 paper is not literally byte-identical. Six source pages were visually inspected. Owned bounded diagnostics completed 2060 checks without failures.
notes.text:
The exact original task and entire family dossier, augmented assignment, all nine actual FINAL note fields, all nine expanded note fields, entire 58826-byte native paper, entire 151629-byte standalone reader, and entire qualified G331 paper, mandatory annotation, source ledger and scope were read. The candidate ledger, scope, coverage and decision, ROOT working proof and B341 source qualifications were treated as unreviewed data. Counts refer to the actual FINAL, not intermediate or expanded notes.

Fresh byte checking found 68/68 current size and SHA-256 matches: 30 mathematical files, five historical evidence files and 33 primary files. Every explicitly reported historical author-owned entry was available: all 15 own files, all 54 input origins and all 54 author-local copies matched afresh. Supplied programs were hashed as bytes and were neither executed nor imported. Unsupplied recursive histories are not represented as freshly checked. Each expanded TeX proof occurs once in both papers and agrees with its expanded native-note text; all nine actual FINAL text fields differ from those expanded texts.

The independent standalone reconstruction is exact after inlining four appendix bodies and replacing both T1 font declarations with the specified fontspec/DejaVu declarations. One substitution occurs inside the verbatim G331 paper. Consequently that embedded paper is mathematically unchanged but not literally byte-identical. The other three embedded grant components are exact. This corrects the literal reader-receipt wording without editing immutable inputs. The four copies in qualified-G331/ remain byte-identical to their originals. The exact original problem matches original-task-statement.txt modulo its trailing newline; that statement plus augmented-assignment.txt reconstructs the author's augmented problem. The original completion criteria remain a prefix of the augmented criteria.

Six freshly rendered source pages were opened visually. SH printed pages 348, 353, 355 and 356 confirm the radical conditions, ambient-degree/factorial convention, finite annihilator in 17.4.6, and invalid unquotiented colon length printed in 17.4.7. In k[[x,y]], (x):y=(x) has infinite length. The valid correction is ((x):y)/(x), equivalently the annihilator of y in the current quotient R/(x), which is zero here. BFJ printed pages 480–481 confirm its generic-colength/sign convention and coefficient-topology upper-semicontinuity argument. Source bodies and pixels remain local.

Owned bounded_checks.py completed 2060 exact arithmetic checks with zero failures: 25 diagonal cases, 625 mixed-area cases, 625 moment-symmetry cases, 625 product-atom cases, 100 strict-maximum comparisons, 24 contraction minima and 36 residue first differences. The domain comprises axis exponents 1..5, all 625 ordered pairs of the resulting 25 monomial ideals, contraction N=1..24 with exponents 0..2N, and residue d=2,3,5, r=1,2,4, N=1..4. These observations do not prove their geometric interpretation or an arbitrary-ring theorem. The supplied author's separate 6765-check report was read as data, not rerun or promoted to proof.

Deliverables are whole-proof.md, whole-source-application-ledger.md, independent-review.md, whole-proof-coverage.md, original-scope-and-noncircularity.md, acceptance-decision.json and native-notes.json. Supporting artifacts include qualified-G331/, bounded-input.json, n1.md through n9.md and evidence/. Rerun owned programs from this directory: python review_data.py; python compare_packets.py; python inspect_sources.py; python bounded_checks.py; python assemble_review.py; python final_check.py. Exact inputs, outputs, commands, hashes and environment are retained. Python is 3.12.14 on Linux x86_64. The final consistency audit passed for nine notes, four unchanged grant components and all required deliverables; it establishes artifact consistency only.

No subagent, native model job, supplied executable, compiler, network operation, active P12.5/private output, auth/runtime change, editor mutation, catalogue operation or publication was used. No supervised heavy-compute facility was exposed; none was needed, and no resource-heavy computation was launched. Compilation and external acceptance remain with the operator.

notes.summary: The mixed-multiplicity kernel reconstructs over arbitrary residue fields, including units, repeated and unused labels, and nonpure superficial quotients.
notes.detailedSummary: Whole leading-form equalities establish product/power laws and integral-closure invariance. Simultaneous superficial elements in the same successive quotients establish every-slot monotonicity. R(z) preserves actual dimension and finite lengths. Stabilized colons give finite current annihilators rather than the invalid literal SH 17.4.7 expression. Top-form exact-sequence additivity includes lower-dimensional zero contributions.
notes.text:
Let R be the positive-dimensional excellent reduced local ring, n=dim R, and let I_j be proper maximal-primary ideals. For a finite module M, the eventual polynomial length of M/(product I_j^s_j)M has degree dim M. Its ambient degree-n form H_M has coefficients e(I_1^[d_1],...,I_r^[d_r];M)/product d_j! for sum d_j=n; H_M=0 when dim M<n. In n separately labelled slots the mixed multiplicity is the coefficient of s_1...s_n. These conventions also apply in the possibly nonreduced successive quotients. A unit variable is absent, and a coefficient using it is zero.

Unused-label deletion cannot be obtained by substituting exponent zero into an eventual polynomial. Fix its exponent at a large c and choose another primary K with K^N contained in B^c. For the remaining product P_s, P_s K^N is contained in B^c P_s, which is contained in P_s. The two outer length polynomials have the same highest form because their exponents differ by a constant. Dividing along every positive rational ray by its parameter to the power n squeezes the middle highest form to that form. Equality on all positive rational rays is polynomial identity. Its degree-n terms in the remaining variables are precisely those with unused-label exponent zero.

Variable permutation proves symmetry. Substituting l s for an exponent proves the I^l law. To split IJ, introduce separate I,J labels and then identify their variables. In the selected first-power coefficient their two degrees sum to one; only the two individual contributions remain, with unused labels deleted as just proved. Thus e(IJ,K_2,...,K_n)=e(I,K_2,...,K_n)+e(J,K_2,...,K_n). Merging repeated equal labels by the sum of their variables gives the stated factorial convention. Unit factors contribute zero.

If I is contained in J and J is integral over I, homogeneous integral equations make R[Jt] finite graded over R[It]. Generators of bounded degrees give J^(m+c) contained in I^m. For m>c, I^m P_s is contained in J^m P_s, which is contained in I^(m-c)P_s. The outer highest forms agree; the rational-ray squeeze proves equality of the entire middle highest form and therefore every mixed coefficient. Equal closures are reduced to this through I+J. This is an equality argument; polynomial nonnegativity would not establish coefficient order, as (s-t)^2 illustrates.

For monotonicity compare J contained in I while keeping all other labels fixed. If needed, pass to T=R[z] localized at mR[z]. Faithful flatness and tensoring a finite-length composition series preserve length exactly: each residue factor becomes k(z). Dimension remains n: n parameters extend to an mT-primary ideal, giving the upper bound by height, and flat going-down from mT lifts an n-chain, giving the lower bound. No valuative-boundary scalar extension is assumed.

Over the infinite residue field, the superficial choices for both compared families exclude finitely many proper linear subspaces. Intersect these open conditions and avoid the current minimal primes. Such avoidance remains possible in nonpure quotients: if a primary ideal K were contained in P+mK, Nakayama on K/(K intersect P) would imply K contained in the minimal prime P, impossible in positive dimension. Choose one x for both families and use the SAME quotient. Its dimension drops by one: any chain in the quotient extends strictly below its first prime to a minimal prime avoiding x; conversely quotient parameters together with x give the height lower bound.

For P_s=product I_j^s_j, multigraded Artin–Rees follows from finite generation of the intersection submodule inside the multigraded Rees module. It gives (P_s:x) contained in (0:x)+P_(s-e). Because all radicals are m, a sufficiently high power of the selected I_1 absorbs the fixed other powers and puts this remainder in the superficial truncated range. Superficiality consequently gives (P_s:x)=(0:x)+P_(s-e_1). The annihilator intersects the truncated range trivially: applying superficiality at arbitrarily large first exponents puts any such element in every power of I_1, hence zero by Krull intersection. Thus (0:x) injects into a finite primary quotient and has finite length.

The multiplication-by-x exact sequence now gives length(R/P_s)-length(R/P_(s-e_1))=length(R/(x,P_s))-length(0:x). In dimension greater than one the annihilator changes only the constant term, so the degree-(d-1) coefficients give the superficial reduction formula. Repeat simultaneous choices in the other selected ideals in the common successive quotients. Embedded primes, nilpotents and nonpure components are permitted. At the final one-dimensional quotient, inclusion of powers gives the correct order of Samuel leading coefficients. This proves every-slot mixed monotonicity and positivity, with units handled separately.

For a short exact sequence of finite modules, multigraded Artin–Rees squeezes the induced intersection between two fixed exponent shifts of the submodule filtration. Their highest forms agree. The exact sequence of induced quotients therefore gives H_M2=H_M1+H_M3. Modules of dimension below n contribute zero.

G331's all-support primary valuative criterion transfers equal rational profiles to equal integral closures of synchronized powers, and profile inequalities to the corresponding mixed-moment order. A positive-dimensional reduced local ring has no zero-dimensional minimal component, so the extra component condition in that criterion causes no omitted case here.

The valid final superficial correction is the length of the annihilator of x_d in M/(x_1,...,x_(d-1))M, equivalently the colon divided by the previous parameter submodule. The literal unquotiented SH 17.4.7 printing is not used. Complete immediate SH units and application hypotheses are recorded in whole-source-application-ledger.md; ordinary recursive historical dependencies are disclosed. The full reconstruction is retained in n2.md and whole-proof.md.

notes.summary: Positive bounded moment measures have all-support representation independence, uniform continuity and prescribed-limit decreasing-NET continuity.
notes.detailedSummary: A positive rational ideal-difference functional extends by the dense lattice and real Riesz representation. Mass and a binomial perturbation bound yield the continuous class. Actual decreasing C representations and an exact majorant-supremum formula yield bounded D, additivity and all required nets. Moment order is never promoted to measure order, and limit membership is required.
notes.text:
Write X=X_a, p=n-1. For rational inputs u_i=-v(I_i)/q_i define B_u(v(J))=e(I_1,...,I_p,J)/product q_i; for p=0 this is e(J). Synchronizing denominators and products represents every rational ideal-difference test as (v(J)-v(K))/d. Equality of two representations is equality of profiles of their cross-products. The closure invariance and product laws of n2 make the proposed values equal, including the unit case. A nonnegative difference gives a primary integral-closure inclusion, so mixed monotonicity gives functional positivity. This proves input and test independence on all supports.

Since 1=v(a), positivity of r+f and r-f for rational r greater than the sup norm gives |B(f)| bounded by ||f|| B(1). G331's separating rational lattice is uniformly dense in real C(X). Rational scalar approximation makes the continuous extension real-linear. Approximating a nonnegative continuous function and adding a vanishing rational error proves positivity. Compact-Hausdorff Riesz therefore supplies a unique finite positive Radon measure with mass e(I_1,...,I_p,a)/product q_i.

Set E_J=e(a^[p],J). Inputs in [-M,0] satisfy 0<=B_u(v(J))<=M^p E_J and mass<=M^p e(a). If two tuples in that range differ uniformly by at most epsilon, the legitimate negative shift in each slot and multilinearity give
|B_u(v(J))-B_w(v(J))| <= ((M+epsilon)^p-M^p) E_J.
Each nonempty shifted-slot subset of size r contributes at most epsilon^r M^(p-r)E_J. Rational upper errors justify the initial rational case; limits give real coefficients. For p=0 the difference bound is zero.

Uniform rational approximation now extends the measure to C tuples independently of the approximations. Symmetry, addition, nonnegative real homogeneity, moment order and the displayed bound pass to the limit. Continuous-test convergence follows by lattice approximation and the common mass bound. Thus this is weak uniform continuity, also for nets.

For bounded D inputs choose any ACTUAL decreasing C representations g_(i,alpha_i) converging to u_i. Every representing term lies in the same [-M,0] bound. On the finite product directed set the ideal moments increase to finite suprema. The limiting lattice functional remains positive and bounded, and Riesz gives its measure and weak convergence.

For another representation f_beta, fixed beta and epsilon>0, the continuous strict sets {g_(i,alpha)<f_(i,beta)+epsilon} form directed covers of compact X. A common index works everywhere in every slot. Moment order and the perturbation bound compare B_fbeta with the first representation's supremum. Let epsilon tend to zero, take sup_beta, and interchange the representations. This proves full representation independence. The same argument gives the exact formula
B_u(v(J))=sup {B_h(v(J)): h_i in C and h_i>=u_i}.
These majorants remain in [-M,0]. Inclusion of majorant sets proves moment order on bounded D, not measure order.

Actual finite-product representations of g_alpha+f_beta decrease to u+w, whose D membership is known from G331. They prove additivity; scaling and symmetry follow in the same way. Zero scaling means the actual zero function. The perturbation estimate consequently holds throughout the established bounded D domain. It proves weak uniform continuity within this domain without assuming increasing-limit closure.

Finally suppose a bounded D net u_(i,lambda) decreases to a SPECIFIED u_i in D. Moment order gives one inequality. For a C majorant tuple h and epsilon>0, the sets {u_(i,lambda)<h_i+epsilon} are open by upper semicontinuity, increase with the directed order, and cover X. Compactness selects a common lambda. Moment order and the perturbation bound yield B_h(v(J))<=B_u_lambda(v(J))+((M+epsilon)^p-M^p)E_J. Taking sup_lambda, then epsilon to zero, then the majorant supremum proves the reverse inequality and exact target convergence. Lattice density and the common mass bound give weak convergence for every continuous test.

This handles arbitrary directed nets and all supports. It invokes no increasing D closure, arbitrary-infimum membership, nested-net flattening or measure-order inference. The rational moments and these continuities uniquely determine the operator. Complete arguments are retained in n3.md and whole-proof.md.

notes.summary: Supported Cartier intersections retain nilpotent thickness, improper-cut symmetry and DVR local degree, with componentwise cycle projection and raw Rees comparison.
notes.detailedSummary: Euler polynomials are constructed by an m-filtration over the residue field, without a coefficient field. Generic lengths include every nilpotent layer. Actual supported Koszul complexes prove full symmetry. Nonpure top-component analysis permits divisor-CYCLE projection before numerical projection. Eventual Rees H0 and Serre vanishing yield the diagonal and mixed identities.
notes.text:
On an actual primary model Y, an effective exceptional Cartier divisor E is killed by a power of m as a coherent scheme. It is proper over the resulting Artinian quotient, and its coherent cohomology has finite R-length. Define chi_R(E,F) by the alternating lengths of this cohomology. Catenary finite-type dimension theory gives dim E<=p=n-1: a component dominating R/P has exceptional-fibre dimension at most dim(R/P)-1. Smaller dominating components cannot supply dimension-p exceptional primes.

Filter O_E by m^j O_E. Each graded quotient is coherent on the proper residue-field scheme E_0 and has support dimension at most p. Tensoring by line bundles is exact. The proper-field Euler-polynomial theorem applied to these quotients therefore makes chi_R(E,O_E tensor product O(F_i)^t_i) a polynomial of total degree at most p. This avoids treating the mixed-characteristic thickening as a k-scheme. Define Q_Y(F_1,...,F_p,E) as its t_1...t_p coefficient. At p=0 it is length H^0(E,O_E), since the proper zero-dimensional Artinian-base scheme is finite.

Generic-length decomposition of the filtered quotients gives
Q_Y(F_1,...,F_p,E)=sum_(dim Z=p) length_(O_Y,eta_Z)(O_E,eta_Z) (O(F_1)|Z ... O(F_p)|Z . Z).
All nilpotent layers contribute to the generic length. Lower-dimensional supports contribute no degree-p coefficient. A fixed extra twist translates variables and preserves this coefficient.

Variable substitutions prove symmetry and additivity in the first p slots. The actual Cartier sequence 0 -> O_E1(-E_2) -> O_(E_1+E_2) -> O_E2 -> 0 proves effective last-slot additivity. The Cartier order unit from G331 expresses any exceptional integral F as a difference of effective divisors; equality of two decompositions is equality of effective sums. This extends Q independently to all integral exceptional divisors and then to the real Cartier tensor group.

Full symmetry uses actual supported Koszul complexes. For effective E,F, their two-term locally free resolutions tensor to the same total complex under interchange. Resolving one first gives complexes on E or F whose terms have finite-length cohomology, even when the induced cut is improper or a zerodivisor. Hypercohomology Euler identities give chi_R(E,L)-chi_R(E,L(-F))=chi_R(F,L)-chi_R(F,L(-E)). The free terms on Y themselves need not have finite length, and no such length is taken. Reading the coefficient of n-2 other variables in this finite difference, using the total-degree bound, exchanges E and F. Differences and real linearity give full symmetry.

This is supported local degree, not global Chow degree: on Spec k[[t]], Q((t))=1 although the principal closed-point class is zero in global CH_0.

For proper refinements and finite normalizations, excellence supplies the universally catenary dimension-function setting. Pullback Cartier equations remain regular on reduced dominating components. At a dimension-p exceptional generic point, smaller components are absent and the local ring B is reduced one-dimensional. The injection into the sum of its minimal-component domains has finite-length cokernel T. For a regular g, the snake sequence and equality length(T[g])=length(T/gT) show length(B/gB)=sum_P length((B/P)/g(B/P)). Thus its top divisor cycle decomposes componentwise with the correct weights.

The proper divisor-CYCLE projection theorem applies on each integral top component: equal dimension-function dimensions, proper dominant map and function-field degree one. Before any Chow quotient it gives f_*[f^*E]_p=[E]_p. Proper-field numerical projection on each exceptional prime then gives zero for lower-dimensional images and the residue-weighted degree for dominating images. Hence Q_Y'(f^*F_1,...,f^*F_n)=Q_Y(F_1,...,F_n).

For a primary ideal I, put D_I=-E_I. The standard finite Rees algebra and eventual Proj section theorem give H^0(Y,O(qD_I))=I^q for large q. Higher Serre vanishing holds simultaneously for q and q-1. The Cartier exact sequence therefore gives length(I^(q-1)/I^q)=chi_R(E_I,O_EI((q-1)D_I)). Leading coefficients yield Q(D_I^[p],E_I)=e(I), equivalently -Q(D_I^[n])=e(I), including p=0.

On a common product blowup, the divisor of product I_j^t_j is sum t_j D_Ij. Its Samuel multiplicity is n! times the degree-n multigraded length form evaluated at t. The diagonal identity on every positive integral t is a polynomial identity. Comparing t_1...t_n coefficients gives -Q(D_I1,...,D_In)=e(I_1,...,I_n). Unit slots vanish.

All newly applied immediate Stacks statements and proofs—0BEL, 0AG7, 01OF, 0AYA, 02QL and 0B5S—were read at their actual hypotheses. Recursive historical foundations are disclosed in whole-source-application-ledger.md. No normality, CM assumption, coefficient field or parameter-colength formula was imposed on this construction. Full details are in n4.md and whole-proof.md.

notes.summary: Independent positive REAL nef atoms are invariant under refinement before algebraic comparison; one fixed primary correction supplies the genuine intersection bridge.
notes.detailedSummary: Normal lifts, equality of DVRs in the same fraction field, exactly-one-prime cycle projection and numerical projection establish atomic invariance. Qualified G331 supplies finite-span real ample approximation. Actual globally generated image ideals satisfy J_q O=O(qL+D0) on one Bl_(I c0), giving both uniform all-support profiles and finite-coefficient intersection convergence. This proves function and primary-model independence.
notes.text:
Normalize a common primary model. On its top normal components, let Z run over the dimension-p exceptional primes, b_Z=ord_Z(a)>0 and nu_Z=ord_Z/b_Z. For negative-effective REAL curve-nef divisors D_1,...,D_p define independently
mu_geom=sum_Z b_Z (D_1|Z ... D_p|Z . Z) delta_nu_Z.
At p=0 the numerical coefficient is [kappa(Z):k]. Closed residue weights are included; no separability is assumed.

Positivity precedes ideal comparison. Precisely qualified G331 proves real nef plus a positive ample perturbation is real ample, finite-span openness, and genuine Q-ampleness of a rational real-ample class. Subtract small positive multiples of E_I and round effective-presentation coefficients upward rationally while retaining ampleness. These negative rational ample divisors converge in a fixed finite coefficient span to D_i. Finite normalization pulls ample bundles to ample bundles, and restriction to a proper Z remains ample. Clearing denominators gives positive mixed intersections; their finite multilinear coefficient limits are nonnegative. Thus the atomic measure is positive by geometric curve-nef reasoning.

For any exceptional real F, evaluation at nu_Z is ord_Z(F)/b_Z. The supported generic-length formula of n4 consequently gives integral H_F dmu_geom=Q_Y(D_1,...,D_p,F).

Refinement invariance is established before algebraic moments. A normalized refinement maps to the old normalization: chart functions integral over the target belong to normal source local rings in the same fraction field; the lifts glue and the graph proves properness. A source prime dominating an old dimension-p prime gives a DVR dominating the target DVR in the SAME fraction field. Writing each field element as t^m times a target unit proves the valuation rings, normalized orders and residue fields equal. The actual divisor-cycle projection of n4, applied to E_I with its positive target coefficient, forces exactly one such source prime over each old prime. Numerical projection preserves its mixed weight; every additional prime with lower-dimensional image has zero p-fold pulled-back intersection. Thus the measure is unchanged under refinements and common normalized lifts.

The comparison requires an actual ideal identity. On fixed Y=Bl_I R, let T=H^0(Y,O_Y). It is finite birational, and T/R is supported at the closed point. Choose h with m^h(T/R)=0 and fix c0=m^(h+1). Then c0 T is contained in m as elements of R. For negative rational ample L and large divisible q, O(qL) is generated and its finite section module F_q lies in T. J_q=c0 F_q is an ideal of R, proper by the displayed containment and unit away from m by localization and the divisor trivialization. Hence it is proper primary.

Use ONE refinement Y'=Bl_(I c0) R. Both I and c0 have invertible regular images there. Global generation gives the exact image F_q O_Y=O(qL) inside O_Y; pullback preserves the surjection and its regular inclusion, because its generator is nonzero on every reduced dominating component. Multiplying the invertible image of c0 gives the ACTUAL identity J_q O_Y'=O_Y'(q f^*L+D0), where D0 is the fixed negative c0 divisor. Universal blowup properties give maps to every Bl_Jq. The same c0 and Y' work for every q and every divisor being approximated.

For simultaneous L_i, the mixed ideal comparison and this image identity give
e(J_(1,q1),...,J_(n,qn))/product q_i = -Q_Y'(f^*L_1+D0/q1,...,f^*L_n+D0/qn).
On every semivaluation support the same image identity gives -v(J_q)/q=H_L-v(c0)/q. The error is uniformly bounded because c0 is PRIMARY. Evaluation uses the support quotient valuation ring and generic trivialization, so no nonminimal support is discarded.

Approximate real core inputs by the negative rational ample L_i in their fixed finite spans and send generated divisible q_i to infinity. The right-hand intersection converges by its fixed-model coefficient polynomial. Separately, the profiles converge uniformly by the primary error bound. The moment continuity of n3 and common mass bound permit the final test to vary uniformly as well. This proves integral H_Dn dmu_alg(H_D1,...,H_Dp)=Q_Y(D_1,...,D_p,D_n). Uniform function convergence alone was not treated as intersection convergence.

An arbitrary exceptional integral F is a difference of two negative ample divisors F-NE_I and -NE_I. Linearity extends the test identity to all real exceptional F. Common refinements allow every primary-ideal test; independent atomic invariance, the supported pairing and the dense lattice identify mu_geom with mu_alg as Radon measures. The measure therefore depends only on the functions and is independent of primary-model and divisor presentations. The bounded C/D extension from n3 is consequently an extension of independently constructed geometry.

Full statements, image arguments, residue conventions and source restrictions are retained in n5.md and whole-proof.md. No arbitrary-proper-model cofinality is asserted.

notes.summary: Bounded ordinary open locality follows from actual ratio-subideal geometry and two justified compact-cover limits.
notes.detailedSummary: Strict inequality at an atom makes one ratio ideal zero on the entire integral exceptional prime and the other line bundle trivial, preserving all mixed weights. Uniform C approximation, fixed-test decreasing limits in other D slots, two successive selected-slot limits and final uniform convergence inside known D establish Radon restriction equality. No plurifine, Borel-cutoff, increasing-closure or measure-order shortcut is used.
notes.text:
For p>=1 synchronize rational selected inputs u=-v(A)/q and w=-v(B)/q. Their maximum is -v(A+B)/q. A common primary product model, followed by normalization, makes A,B,A+B, the other inputs and a reference primary ideal invertible. The reference handles unit cases. Put S=(A+B)O, L=AO/S and M=BO/S. These are ACTUAL invertible subideals of O and satisfy L+M=O.

At an exceptional prime Z where u(nu_Z)>w(nu_Z), ord_Z(A)<ord_Z(B), so ord_Z(M)>0. The map M|Z -> O_Z is zero on the ENTIRE integral reduced Z: in each trivialization its regular generator vanishes generically and hence identically. Restricting L+M=O then makes L|Z surject onto O_Z, so it is a trivial line bundle. Therefore D_A-D_(A+B) restricts trivially on Z. All mixed atomic weights agree there, with the other slots fixed. Since both measures use the same finite divisorial set, mu(max(u,w),others) and mu(u,others) have equal restrictions to {u>w}. This is geometric atomic equality, not moment order.

For C inputs and a fixed continuous test h supported compactly inside the open strict set, continuity gives a positive minimum gap on its support. Sufficiently accurate uniform rational approximants retain that gap. Their identities pass to C by weak uniform continuity. Keep selected u,w in C and h fixed while the other bounded D slots are represented by actual decreasing C nets. Their prescribed-limit continuity extends the identity to all other bounded D slots.

Now let bounded D functions u,w agree on open U and fix h with compact support K contained in U. Choose actual decreasing C representations u_alpha and w_beta with a common bound. For fixed alpha and epsilon>0, the sets {w_beta-epsilon<u_alpha} form a directed open cover of K. Compactness selects beta0; this supplies a fixed open neighborhood of K valid for every later beta. The preceding selected-C identity gives equality of the h-integrals for max(u_alpha,w_beta-epsilon) and u_alpha.

First decrease beta. Its known bounded D limit is max(u_alpha,w-epsilon). Then decrease alpha. The second known bounded D limit is max(u,w-epsilon). Two applications of the prescribed-limit net continuity give integral h dmu(max(u,w-epsilon),others)=integral h dmu(u,others). These are successive limits with a fixed test, not nested-net flattening. Interchanging u and w gives the corresponding identity for w.

Both shifted maxima converge uniformly to the ALREADY KNOWN bounded D function max(u,w), with error at most epsilon. Although this family may increase as epsilon decreases, no increasing-limit membership is needed: apply uniform continuity within the established domain. The two right-hand integrals are therefore equal.

These compactly supported continuous tests determine Radon restrictions to U. Compact-Hausdorff normality gives cutoffs supported in U and equal to one on any chosen compact subset. Inner regularity identifies open-subset masses as suprema of their integrals; equality then extends to Borel restrictions. Replacing slots successively gives full mixed locality. At p=0 locality is automatic.

This proves ordinary OPEN locality on the full normalized boundary. It does not claim plurifine locality or arbitrary Borel-cutoff locality. Complete arguments are retained in n6.md and whole-proof.md.

notes.summary: Gauge, full normalization/conductor, curve Cartier comparison and degenerate cases survive with exact residue weights.
notes.detailedSummary: The gauge measure transforms with one factor, independently of dimension. Finite normalization uses top-degree exact-sequence additivity and closed residue degrees, including inseparability. Lower-dimensional components contribute zero without deleting their points. Every curve primary model has the correct zero-arity Cartier degree. Empty, unit, zero, bottom and nonreduced conventions are explicit.
notes.text:
For another primary gauge b put d(v)=v_a(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v). Transport inputs by u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). G331 gives the homeomorphism and bounded continuous d,d^-1. Testing T_*[d mu_a] against v_b(J) cancels exactly the test denominator and yields the unchanged rational mixed moment. Density proves mu_b=T_*[d mu_a]. There is ONE weight factor, independent of n. Transported C and bounded decreasing D representations and weak continuity extend this formula. The new mass is the old moment against v_a(b); rationally it is e(I_1,...,I_p,b)/product q_i. The factors obey d_ab(v)d_bc(T_ab v)=v_a(c), giving the exact cocycle. Geometric atoms give the same law directly because their b_Z changes from ord_Z(a) to ord_Z(b).

Let S be finite normalization. A regular conductor element kills S/R, and a chain above a prime in its support extends strictly below to a minimal prime avoiding that element. Thus dim(S/R)<n. Top-form exact-sequence additivity gives H_R=H_S.
